question.worked_solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $-11$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

Using the addition rule, then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{x}-11) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-11) \\  & =9\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & =9{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
